For a buyer the practical points are the form bought, the basis a result is reported on, where the soybean Oil came from and the laboratory’s reporting limit. Testing finds contamination but does not remove it.

<div class="hmi-analyte-explorer" id="hmi-occurrence-soybean-oil" data-analyte-explorer data-compact-intro="true" data-source-summaries="true"><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-explorer-context><summary data-open-context aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-controls="hmi-occurrence-soybean-oil-drawer">Comparison methods and scope</summary><div data-explorer-context-content>

<p>Each row is one statistic a source reports for one form of soybean oil, group and metal; percentiles, ranges and maxima reported for the same samples as a mean or median are shown on that row. Different forms and preparation states are kept apart, and dry-weight results never share a reference with as-sold or fresh-weight results. Ratings place a result against an HMI reference built from monitoring results and ordinary-setting medians for the same form and basis. Same-study contrasts compare a contaminated or treated site with its control, targeted with random sampling, a prepared form with the unprocessed one, or one group of a study with the median of its other groups. Held rows failed a check against their own source and are shown but not compared.</p>

<a id="sources-and-contamination-pathways"></a>
## How metals reach soybean Oil

<a id="hmi-ing-010"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-supports-root-uptake-surface-deposition-feed-transfer-or-other-biological-pathways"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-011"></a>
<a id="what-contamination-can-arise-from-agricultural-inputs-harvesting-processing-equipment-or-packaging"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-012"></a>
<a id="which-source-attribution-claims-are-measured-modelled-inferred-or-unresolved"></a>

The evidence on how metals reach soybean Oil comes from studies that compared exposed and ordinary settings. Soybean Oil, oil from factory A crude oil (A1) had nickel higher at 550 µg/kg, against 10 µg/kg for factory A refined oil (A2) in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/onoja2025-makurdi-crude-refined-soybean-oil|6]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Onoja AJ, Muyong MG, Bongjo NB · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/onoja2025-makurdi-crude-refined-soybean-oil">Quality and Safety of Soybean Oils in Makurdi: Physicochemical Properties, Contaminants, and Residues</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">American Journal of Food Science and Technology 4(2), 9-14</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/onoja2025-makurdi-crude-refined-soybean-oil">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> In another study, soybean Oil, oil from extraction had cadmium higher at 150 µg/kg, against 20 µg/kg for pressed bleached oil, fraction 4, one production lot in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/authors2016-a-comparative-study-of-the-content-of-heavy|9]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Unknown authors · 2016</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/authors2016-a-comparative-study-of-the-content-of-heavy">A comparative study of the content of heavy metals in oils:</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Peer-reviewed article</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/authors2016-a-comparative-study-of-the-content-of-heavy">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

These are observational comparisons from single studies; the size of the difference depends on the site, metal and distance.

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="how-much-of-the-arsenic-in-soybean-oil-is-inorganic" data-anchor="how-much-of-the-arsenic-in-soybean-oil-is-inorganic" data-question="How much of the arsenic in soybean Oil is inorganic?">
